model capabilities.why: What a model can do is read from the catalogue, never guessed from its name.

route ids.why: A surface that invents its own route prefix sends a signed-in reader somewhere the middleware does not know about.

plan ids.why: A plan name spelled twice becomes two products the day one of them is renamed.

entitlements.why: What a plan buys is one list; a client that keeps its own decides access without the server.

credit conversion.why: One rate turns money into credits. A second copy prices the same work differently on two surfaces.

usage accounting.why: Which bucket a request spends from decides when a reader is cut off, so it cannot be a per-surface opinion.

role names.why: A role is what a principal holds on a resource; a surface that invents one grants something nothing enforces.

permission names.why: A permission the server never heard of is a control that renders and does nothing.

error codes.why: A reader is told what went wrong by code, not by parsing the sentence a server happened to write.

feature ids.why: A feature is gated at named layers; a surface that invents a layer gates nothing.

tool schemas.why: One tool shape reaches every surface from the protocol crate, so a member added on one side cannot go missing on the other.

event schemas.why: An event name is a contract with every consumer; a private verb is an event nobody subscribes to.
event schemas.scanWhy: The verbs are ordinary words (started, completed, failed), so a literal match is evidence of a lifecycle status, not of a private copy of the event vocabulary. DOMAIN_EVENT_NAME_PATTERN is what polices a real event name.

sync rules.why: Which objects sync, and how a conflict resolves, is one answer for every device.
sync rules.scanWhy: The object types are the product nouns themselves (message, project, settings), so every surface names them for ordinary reasons.

approval classes.why: When a tool needs a human is a policy the workspace sets, not a default a surface picks.

trust modes.why: Where data may live is the promise the product sells; a surface that restates it can promise something the router will not keep.

interaction modes.why: Chat and agent work are two modes with different budgets and different approvals, named once.
interaction modes.scanWhy: Chat and agent work are two members, and a private copy of a two-member vocabulary is indistinguishable from naming one of them. The registry owns it; the restatement scan cannot see it.

lifecycle state names.why: What a unit of work is doing is one vocabulary; a private spelling is a state no other surface can render.

tool support.why: Whether a tool is available is the server's answer, and a client that decides it shows a control that fails.

error classifications.why: Why a capability was refused decides what the reader is offered next.

provider identity.why: A provider list copied into a surface goes stale the day one is added, and the surface silently drops it.

ownershipGaps.why: Nothing in the tree classifies data by sensitivity. Residency (DATA_REGION_IDS) answers where data may live and the trust modes answer who may hold it, but no vocabulary says how sensitive a given row is.
ownershipGaps.fix: Introduce the classification vocabulary together with the first surface that acts on it, so it is not a vocabulary on paper.

ids.why: What may be an identifier is one rule set, applied to every primary key in the schema.

enums.why: The product nouns are enumerated once, so a surface cannot invent a thirteenth concept nobody stores.

api inputs.why: A request shape parsed by the same schema on both sides cannot drift between the caller and the route.

api outputs.why: A response shape the client parses is the contract; a route that returns something else fails at the boundary rather than in the UI.

error envelope.why: Every failure reaches a reader in the same envelope, classified, so a surface can decide what to offer next.

events.why: An event name is namespaced and verb-shaped, checked by a pattern rather than by convention.

capability manifest.why: What a surface can do is answered by the host and the server together, in one shape both sides version.

model capabilities.why: What a model supports is read from the catalogue, never inferred from its id.

tool schema.why: One tool shape for every surface, owned by the protocol crate and generated into TypeScript.

entitlements.why: Which subscription states buy access is one list; a second copy sells the product twice.

policy schema.why: What an administrator can turn off is enumerated, so a control that renders has something behind it.

sync messages.why: A peer on an older protocol is told it is out of date instead of meeting a parse failure.

remote-control protocol.why: A host and a controller negotiate one version before either acts on the other.

usage events.why: Which bucket a request spends from, and in what order buckets are drawn down, is one answer for every surface.

audit event metadata.why: What an audit row carries is one shape, so a compliance export is complete whatever wrote the row.
